workflow_hypothesis: Concurrent permanent-retention transition races with owner reference counting
pattern: Concurrent non-atomic mutation or initialization of concurrency-visible object metadata races with ownership and lifecycle inspection
description: A shared or newly reachable object exposes ownership, reference-count, lifecycle, or validity metadata to concurrent threads while another operation changes multiple metadata fields or bulk-initializes storage. The cluster covers two related mechanisms: lifecycle promotion can overlap owner reference-count activity or publication, while allocation-time bulk clearing can overlap lock-free header inspection.
precondition: An object can be reached or inspected concurrently, and its concurrency-visible metadata is accessed through a mixture of ordinary stores, atomic operations, locks, or bulk memory writes that are not governed by one consistent synchronization protocol.
critical_operation: One thread either promotes the object to a stronger retention state while rewriting ownership or reference-count metadata, or initializes an allocation by bulk-clearing memory that includes the object header before explicit header initialization is complete.
interference: During that operation, another thread may acquire or release references, inspect ownership or lifecycle state, observe the object through a shared pool, or perform lock-free validation of the header.
invalid_assumption: The implementation assumes that same-thread completion of initialization, atomicity of individual readers, or later correction of metadata makes the transition safe, even though non-atomic multi-field updates or byte-wise bulk writes can overlap concurrent metadata access.
failure: Observers can see mixed, transient, or inconsistent ownership, reference-count, retention, or validity metadata, causing incorrect lifecycle decisions, corrupted reference state, a real data race, memory-safety failure, or process termination. The reports do not establish that the common failure must involve stale or freed state.
search_strategy: Inspect shared-object retention or lifecycle-promotion paths for non-atomic writes to ownership, reference-count, or state fields that can overlap owner-thread reference operations.
Check that publication, lookup, promotion, and cleanup of pooled objects use one compatible lock or atomic-access discipline, and that reference-count adjustments are thread-safe.
Search allocation and reuse paths for memset, zeroing, or other bulk writes that cover concurrency-visible headers before those headers are initialized.
Verify that lock-free readers cannot inspect header metadata during bulk initialization, and that fields read atomically are also written atomically or protected by the same synchronization protocol.

evidence.supports: Shows that promoting an object owned by another thread can race with that owner's reference-count operations; safe handling requires ownership or merged-reference checks and atomic stores for metadata observed concurrently.
Shows that a lifecycle-classification field changed during retention promotion must use atomic reads and writes when other threads can inspect it.

Shows that insertion, promotion, and reference-count adjustment need coordinated locking and thread-safe decrements so another thread cannot observe or use an object during a partially completed transition.
Shows that non-atomic full-allocation clearing can race with concurrent reads of ownership and reference metadata, including transient header values that appear valid or match another thread.

scope_note: This mixed cluster supports an umbrella pattern about unsynchronized writes to concurrency-visible object metadata. Issues 113956, 128137, and 129701 concern pooled-object publication and retention-state promotion; issue 130019 concerns allocation-time bulk initialization of headers. The evidence does not support conflating leaked ownership with stale or freed state, nor claiming that every reference-count race or allocator memset has this form.
